Key Message 1...Mainly dry weather continues through tonight. 

NW'erly flow aloft and stabilizing subsidence affect our region
today as a surface high pressure ridge affects the eastern 
Great Lakes and vicinity, while the ridge aloft builds from the 
Upper Midwest and vicinity. As a result, dry weather is expected
in all of Western and Central NY. Clear to partly cloudy sky 
and weak or calm surface winds will contribute to lows reaching 
the mid 40's to near 60F in the Eastern Lake Ontario Region and 
mainly the 50's to lower 60's elsewhere in our CWA around 
daybreak this morning. The coolest lows are expected in Lewis 
County, especially the Black River Valley, where efficient 
radiational cooling should be complemented by cool air drainage 
from adjacent higher terrain. Sufficient nocturnal cooling and 
low-level moisture will result in patchy radiation fog and 
steam fog in the river and lake valleys of the Western Southern 
Tier, Finger Lakes, and Eastern Lake Ontario Region through 
shortly after daybreak. High temperatures late this afternoon 
are expected to reach the 70's in the Eastern Lake Ontario 
Region and the mid 70's to mid 80's elsewhere.

The ridge at the surface and aloft begins to exit E'ward tonight
as a shortwave trough approaches from the central Great Lakes
and a surface warm front approaches from the OH Valley and
vicinity. Moist isentropic ascent ahead of the shortwave trough
axis and along the upper-reaches of the warm front should 
release weak, yet sufficient elevated CAPE to allow isolated 
showers and thunderstorms to impact the Western Southern Tier 
during the predawn hours of Sunday morning. Fair weather is 
expected to persist elsewhere in our CWA. Lows should reach the 
mid 40's to lower 60's in the Eastern Lake Ontario Region and 
mainly the lower to mid 60's elsewhere. Readings should begin to
moderate toward daybreak, especially in Western NY and the 
Finger Lakes, as low-level WAA strengthens ahead of the warm 
front. 

Key Message 2...Scattered showers and thunderstorms are 
expected Sunday into Sunday night. Isolated showers and 
thunderstorms are possible this Monday.

Cyclonic W'erly to NW'erly flow aloft and embedded shortwave
troughs will impact Western and Central NY on Sunday through
Monday. At the surface, a low should wobble SE'ward from the
northern Great Lakes to near southern New England and Long
Island. This low track should allow the surface warm front to
drift NE'ward through our CWA Sunday morning through evening,
which will usher-in a warmer and more humid air mass originating
over the Gulf, and be followed by the E'ward passage of a 
surface cold front Sunday evening through Monday morning. Behind
the cold front, a surface ridge attempts to build from the 
Upper Midwest and vicinity.

Scattered showers and thunderstorms with periods of heavy
rainfall are expected along and ahead of the surface warm and 
cold fronts as weak to perhaps moderate CAPE, including elevated
CAPE, amidst moderate to perhaps strong deep-layer bulk shear, 
is released by the following: moist isentropic ascent along the
upper-reaches of the warm front, low-level convergence/moist 
ascent along the surface warm and cold fronts, and as downshear 
gust fronts interact favorably with low-level vertical wind 
shear. Severe storms still appear possible Sunday afternoon into
the evening, but their occurrence will be contingent on 
multiple factors, including the degree of diurnal 
destabilization of the warm/moist sector boundary layer. 
Sufficient diurnal destabilization for severe storm occurrence 
remains questionable given the expectation of abundant cloud 
cover on Sunday. Behind the cold front, isolated rain showers 
should occur Sunday night into Monday since subtle shortwave 
troughs and attendant surface trough axes will traverse Western 
and Central NY generally from west to east. Low-level convergence
and moist ascent along the surface trough axes should release 
at least weak potential instability in the lowest ~1 km AGL. A 
few thunderstorms are possible Monday afternoon and evening, 
before sunset, when the same lifting mechanisms may release weak
boundary layer CAPE stemming from daytime warming. Compared to 
24-hours ago, the potential for lake-effect rain showers over 
and generally southeast of Lakes Erie and Ontario overnight 
Sunday night into Monday appears to be marginal since post-cold
front low-level CAA may be slightly weaker than projected by 
previous cycles of NWP models. We will continue to monitor the 
potential for lake-effect rain.

High temperatures are forecast to reach the 70's to lower 80's
Sunday afternoon. Lows should reach mainly the upper 50's to 
mid 60's around daybreak Monday. Late afternoon highs should 
reach the 70's to lower 80's on Monday, behind the weak cold 
front.

Key Message 3...Dry weather is expected this Monday night
through Tuesday.
